items.justification: Update notification to the user versus inter-system permission scoping.
Prompt remediation and dissemination of threat information to staff are different objectives that together determine how fast an organization actually responds.
Credential uniqueness and protection of sensitive data are distinct objectives that jointly prevent unauthorized access to what the system holds.
Both give the user visibility and control over their personal data, A through deletion instructions and B through disclosure of how data is used and stored.
Prohibition on hard-coded credentials versus patch provision and delivery.
Disabling unused interfaces versus justifying undocumented components.
Vetted cryptographic implementations versus a general threat-modelling process that applies to every control alike.
Deletion of data from associated services versus supplier due diligence.
Brute-force resistance versus staff threat awareness.
Vulnerability disclosure policy versus secure disposal on ownership transfer.
B's threat modelling explicitly covers data poisoning, the class of attack A's input validation defends against; the process and the control serve the same risk.
Setup guidance versus incident support.
Recording unmet provisions versus data and input sanitisation.
Vetted cryptographic implementations versus monitoring internal model states.
Authenticated configuration change versus performance monitoring.
Both create a security-relevant record of what happened to the system, A by alerting on tampering and B by logging actions for investigation.
Secure boot versus a generic threat-modelling process not specific to boot integrity.
Password uniqueness versus cost-based prioritisation of identified risks.
Securing one's own development process and assessing externally sourced components are distinct duties that together determine the security of the delivered software.
Setup verification guidance versus disaster recovery planning.
Verifying incoming updates and logging configuration changes are separate objectives that together account for how a deployed system came to be in its current state.
Authentication cryptography versus component justification.
Checking for available updates and giving advance notice of updates are different obligations that together keep the user informed and current.
Both apply least privilege; A to the privileges software runs with, B to permissions the system holds on other systems, with an added risk assessment.
Vetted implementations versus role-tailored security training.
Both make security documentation available to others, but the disclosure policy and the design audit trail serve different assurance purposes.
User control over automatic updates versus permission scoping.
Uniqueness of security parameters versus human oversight capability.
Ease of applying updates versus disaster recovery planning.
Timely vulnerability remediation versus content requirements for system documentation.
User setup guidance versus re-testing after major system updates.
Ease of applying an update and advance notice that one is coming are different obligations that together govern the user's experience of updating.
Communication cryptography versus disclosure of data handling.
Automatable update mechanism versus independent security testing.
Brute-force resistance versus a generic threat-modelling process.
Vetted cryptographic implementations versus data and input sanitisation.
Publishing replacement support versus internal involvement of Data Custodians.
Installation usability versus incident support.
Automatic update activation versus guidance on model limitations.
Both frustrate attacks that scale automatically: A by making parameters unique per device, B by rate-limiting API access to slow reverse engineering and poisoning.
